This image tells the powerful story of Tony Robbins, one of the most influential life coaches in the world today. His beginning was far from easy. 

He grew up in a violent household and was forced out of his home at just 17. Before his breakthrough, he struggled with being overweight, depressed, and completely broke. He never even attended college.

But Tony refused to let his circumstances decide his future. He dug deep, committed to changing his life, and eventually turned his pain into purpose. 

Through relentless self-education and massive action, he built a multimillion-dollar self-help empire and became known globally as the King of Life Coaches. 👑✨

His journey is a reminder that your story can change the moment you decide to change yourself. 

No excuses. No limits.

Campaigning for the Melaka state election has officially kicked off following Nomination Day last Saturday. Polling Day will be on the 14th of November, which will see 79 candidates vying for 28 seats. Several of the seats will see Barisan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan contesting directly against each other. This state polls will further test the cooperation between BN and PAS, after a resounding victory in Negeri Sembilan in August. What can the Melaka election tell us about the country’s next political chapter? On this episode of #ConsiderThis Melisa Idris (@MelisaMelina_Idris) speaks with Ibrahim Suffian, Programmes Director of Merdeka Center, and Dr Bridget Welsh, honorary research associate at University of Nottingham Malaysia’s Asia Research Institute.
